sn11.4:1.3: Vepacitti (“wise thinker”) was the lord of the _asuras_ and Sakka’s counterpart; their relationship status is complicated. The Sanskrit form is _vipracitti_, but in Buddhist texts it is incorrectly Sanskritized to _vemacitra_. He seems not to appear in early Sanskrit texts, but the Mahābhārata and Purāṇas regard him as the eldest son of Danū and hence chief of the Dānavas.
sn11.4:1.9: It seems they had strong feelings about each other.
sn11.4:1.10: Mātali is the charioteer of Sakka, a role he plays throughout Brahmanical literature as well. He appears at [dn20:10.8]() as one of the centaur lords, and is father to the centaur Sikhaṇḍī, Pañcasikha’s rival in love ([dn21:1.6.8]()). He appears only once in the Rig Veda (10.14.3), but is not explicitly connected with Indra and chariots until Atharva Veda 11.6.23. He is never addressed with the usual word for charioteer (_sārathi_), but by the epithet _saṅgāhaka_, literally “gatherer” in the sense “one who holds the reins”, here “chariot handler”, recalling the centaur who took the reins from Indra (Rig Veda 1.163.2).
sn11.4:7.3: In this tricky phrase, I take _sadatthaparamā atthā_ as truncated dative of purpose. This phrase parallels [sn11.8:3.4]().
